source.title: DUET: Distilled LLM Unlearning from an Efficiently Contextualized Teacher
source.authors: Yisheng Zhong; Zheng-Bang Yang; Zhuangdi Zhu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a newly proposed parameter-based unlearning method withstands reverse-prompt and jailbreak attacks, using its own unlearning and utility evaluations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attacks on DUET and an in-context-unlearned teacher, along with DUET's forgetting and utility results. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Prior work on relearning and attacks is cited but is not this study's result. No specific chance level is stated for the reported forgetting metrics.
record.test_reason: The study proposes DUET, a counter-method (F) claiming robustness. Its own results test whether DUET forgets with utility kept (A) and whether prompt attacks recover knowledge (E). These are a reverse 'ignore previous instructions' prompt (Table 6) and educational/fanfic jailbreaks on DUET, FLAT, GA and SimNPO (Table 17). No fine-tuning, activation-ablation or quantization attacks are run.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. One correction: the main Conclusion claims DUET is robust under reverse-prompt attacks and format shifts, and does not mention jailbreak vulnerability. The admission that DUET 'remains vulnerable to jailbreak attacks' appears only in Appendix A.10.
record.recipe_differences: DUET trains a student by distilling top-K logits from an in-context-unlearning teacher; it is not the gradient-ascent, WHP, or RMU recipe. The paper reports a code repository intended to contain the implementation and results.
record.method_sensitivity: Reverse-prompt robustness differs between the in-context teacher and DUET; jailbreak attack success differs by prompt category. The paper also reports that teacher-prefix quality changes forgetting and retention.
record.problems: The reported Harry Potter forgetting measure is ROUGE-L rather than accuracy, and the paper does not state chance-level references for the reported forgetting metrics. Attack success is judged by an LLM; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other baseline comparisons, prompt-prefix ablations, multi-teacher tests, and training hyperparameter sweeps are omitted because they do not directly test recovery by the attacks named in the claim. The paper also reports content-completion evaluation-format results in Table 7, but not as a recovery attack.

untested.parts: Only DUET faces the reverse-prompt attack; baselines face only jailbreaks. No relearning, ablation or quantization attacks are run.
Entirely untested; no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Entirely untested; no activation-direction ablation or deletion-vs-blocking analysis.
Other languages, in-context information and paraphrase-only attacks are not tested. The reverse prompt is tested only on DUET and the prompt-based teacher.
DUET's robustness to fine-tuning, internal-edit and quantization attacks is not tested.

missing.what: DUET forgetting and utility on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (R-forget 30.04→14.15, MMLU 65.48→65.29) and Mistral-7B-Instruct (48.40→19.57, MMLU 59.74→58.90)
Baseline methods' (GA, NPO, SimNPO, FLAT, RMU) forget/utility values, needed to see which method was attacked in Table 17 and at what forgetting level

record.verdict_notes: The record used version codes V1/V5/V6; these are mapped to A/E/F. Jailbreak ASR has no unattacked baseline, so jailbreak recovery cannot be separated from residual leakage. DUET's R-Forget-500 is reported as 5.98 (Table 1) and as 4.86 in other tables. The reverse-prompt contrast compares DUET with a prompt-only unlearner, not with weight-based baselines.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish a chance-level reference for its forgetting measures; its main Harry Potter measure is ROUGE-L, and it does not test every unlearning method against the attacks.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is run.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis that tests whether knowledge was deleted versus access-blocked is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is reported.
Tests a reverse prompt and two jailbreak prompt categories; does not test other languages or in-context information.
Tests DUET against reverse-prompt and jailbreak attacks, not fine-tuning, internal edits, or quantization attacks.

source_check.notes: Appendix tables (9/12/15/16/18) report DUET as R-Forget-500 4.86, MMLU 61.52, shift 57.09, but Tables 1/4/5/6 give 5.98, 61.45, 55.90. A.10 says three methods but Table 17 lists four, and it does not name the jailbreak model. R-Retain is ROUGE-L on the authors' own 100-QA Dreval set. DUET distils a first-token refusal teacher. Five statements cite this study's rows without saying anything about it.

statements.correction: DUET (own method, Zephyr-7B, WMDP Acc on 500 sampled test items): Bio 63.70->29.40, Cyber 43.68->26.60; MMLU 58.12->60.63 (Bio run), 60.65 (Cyber run) (Table 2). No attack on these checkpoints. ICLR 2026.
statements.problem: Cites r7,r9 but never names DUET or gives its numbers; the 'why' says 'All four', counting only the other studies.

statements.correction: DUET R-forget (ROUGE-L): Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct 32.13->4.27 (Table 1, r2); Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct 30.04->14.15 (Table 13); Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 48.40->19.57 (Table 14). Qwen/Mistral have no rows.
statements.problem: Cites r2 but says nothing about DUET; the DUET model-family contrast it could support is not stated.

statements.correction: DUET (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, HP 500 QA): reverse 'ignore any previous instructions' prompt R-Forget-500 5.98->7.27 (Table 6). Same authors' educational/fanfic jailbreaks: overall ASR 35.62% (FLAT 37.53%), LLM judge, no unattacked baseline; authors say DUET 'remains vulnerable to jailbreak attacks' (A.10, Table 17).
statements.problem: Cites r13 without naming DUET. 'Little or no prompt recovery under own authors' attacks' holds for DUET only under the reverse prompt; the same authors' jailbreak test found it still vulnerable.

statements.correction: Table 17 (100 MUSE forget questions rewritten as educational/fanfic jailbreaks, 10 samples each, LLM judge): no unattacked ASR, retrain or never-trained control. ASR fanfic/educational/overall: DUET 35.05/36.18/35.62, FLAT 44.26/30.79/37.53, GA 45.25/34.26/39.76, SimNPO 49.80/38.02/43.91%.
statements.problem: Cites r14,r16,r19,r22,r23 but never mentions this study's jailbreak test or its missing reference.

statements.correction: This paper's F result: DUET (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct) under reverse prompt R-Forget-500 5.98->7.27, against prefix teacher 4.52->37.62 (Table 6). Either state it as a fifth study or drop the r13 citation.
statements.problem: Its 'DUET' is a benchmark in AdaPop's study, not this paper. This paper has no paraphrase test or AdaPop, yet r13 is cited. 'All four are preprints' excludes this ICLR paper.
